The following amends Claim 6660215639, after the dev's read-only measurement on `origin/main` `fa9c0aa2`.

  - The `from_name` default `'ObjectStack'` in `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/mail.manifest.ts:109`, plus its four-language help text, was already covered by `packages/services/**`.
- **Row 3 shape (seat ruling):**
  - Drop the manifest default, as #25347 did for `workspace_name`.
  - `EmailService` names an unnamed default sender by the same chain the auth mail subject reads: `branding.workspace_name`, then the `OS_APP_NAME` chain, then `ObjectStack`.
  - The plugin binds `branding.workspace_name` the way auth does and follows its changes.
  - An explicit sender name always wins.
- **Row 2: seat ruling A, no change in this PR.** The bulk-import set-password link and the public password-reset link use the same better-auth token and the same setting (`emailAndPassword.resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn`, default 3600 s). The invitation link is a different capability: membership only, signed in, email-matched, no credential set.
  - Lengthening a no-login credential link is a security-boundary choice, the security seat is vacant, and the card's suggested 48 h is not backed by any declared rule.
  - So this PR is `Part of #30212`. Row 2 goes back to the queue as a decision at landing. The options and readings are in `/mnt/project-files/server-seat5/measure-30212-row2.md`.
- **Serial note:** another seat's work on #30208 row 8 (plugin-email status text) may touch `packages/plugins/plugin-email/**`. Whichever PR lands second merges `origin/main`.

Rows 1, 3 and 4 have landed. Row 2 is released back to the queue as a maintainer decision.

## Row 2: needs a ruling

The bulk-import set-password link lasts 60 minutes; invitations last 48 hours. Measured on `origin/main` `fa9c0aa2`, better-auth 1.7.12, read only:
- The import link is the same token kind as the public forgot-password link (`admin-import-users.ts:824` calls `requestPasswordReset`; only the mail template differs). One setting, `EmailAndPasswordConfig.resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn` (default 3600 s, deployment config only), governs both.
- Invitations: better-auth's `invitationExpiresIn` default, 48 h. objectstack never sets it.
- The capabilities differ. The set-password link is an unauthenticated, single-use bearer link that sets the account's first credential; a completed reset revokes the account's other sessions, but a newer mint does not void an older outstanding link. Accepting an invitation needs a signed-in session whose email matches, and sets no credential.

Options:
- **A.** Keep 60 minutes; the administrator re-sends when a link lapses. This is the seat's interim ruling.
- **B.** Import-only lifetime (e.g. 48 h): extend that one verification row's expiry in the import send callback. Public forgot-password stays 60 minutes; no spec key. The mail template needs an hours/days wording (4 locales). Cost: a credential-setting bearer link lives 48x longer in the mailbox.
- **C.** Raise the global default. It also lengthens every public forgot-password link. Not recommended.
- **D.** A new configurable import lifetime. That is a new spec key.

The card's own note asks for the security seat's view on any lifetime change; that seat is vacant, so this goes to the maintainer.

domain:server#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYVV6fcAQrNTDQRvPb

To: security#1 · 2026-11-05T16:39Z

Row 2 of this card needs a security-seat judgment before it goes to the maintainer. The card's own note asks for it: 「Row 2 changes how long a credential-setting link lives, so the dev should confirm the lifetime with the security seat rather than assume it.」 My landing comment above routed it to the maintainer because I took the security seat to be vacant; it is seated, so it comes to you first.

This is a product policy question on a public card, not a finding: nothing here is undisclosed.

The question: should the set-password link a bulk-imported account receives keep the 60-minute lifetime it shares with public forgot-password, or get a longer import-only lifetime (e.g. 48 h, to match invitations)?

The measurement and options A/B/C/D are in the landing comment above. In short:
- **A.** Keep 60 minutes. This is the seat's interim ruling.
- **B.** Import-only lifetime, e.g. 48 h. Public forgot-password stays at 60 minutes and no spec key is added. The cost is a single-use bearer link that sets the first credential and lives 48x longer in a mailbox. A newer mint does not void an older outstanding link.
- **C.** Raise the global default. Not recommended.
- **D.** A configurable import lifetime, which adds a new spec key.
- **E.** (added by the decision thread) Keep 60 minutes and change only the import mail's last line. Today the `auth.account_invitation` mail ends 「如果链接已失效，请联系 {{inviter.name}}」 (`plugin-email/src/templates/auth-templates.ts:492/501`, zh `:518/527`, ja/es the same). Yet the self-serve path already works for an imported account: an expired link opens `ResetPasswordPage.tsx:90-101`, which shows "invalid or expired" with a "get a new link" button into forgot-password. The administrator has no "re-send set-password mail" action, only set-user-password. E rewrites that line in all four locales to point first at getting a new link, then at the administrator. It changes nothing on the security surface.

One more gap if B is chosen: because a newer mint does not void older tokens, an employee who uses forgot-password instead would leave the 48-hour import link alive. B would need "a completed password set voids the account's other unused tokens" in the same card.

Please give your pick (and any condition, e.g. B only with older links voided on re-send) as a comment here. Seat 5 dispatches the implementation from your answer, or carries it to the maintainer if you say it needs his ruling.
